After this the part ‘ghayru uli al-darar’ was revealed. In another chain of al-Bukhari the name of Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) has come as the scribe.

quiz.q: To whom did Quraysh repeatedly take their complaint to stop the da‘wah?
o: To his wife Khadijah (RA)
To his uncle Abu Talib
To his grandfather ‘Abd al-Muttalib
To his uncle Hamzah (RA)
quiz.e: Abu Talib was the chief of Banu Hashim and the protector of the Prophet ﷺ; so Quraysh took pressure consistently to him alone.

quiz.q: The third time, whom did Quraysh want to give to Abu Talib in exchange?
o: The son of Abu Jahl
Khalid ibn al-Walid
‘Umarah ibn al-Walid
‘Amr ibn Hisham
quiz.e: Offering the strong, handsome youth ‘Umarah ibn al-Walid as a son, they asked in exchange for the Prophet ﷺ to kill; Abu Talib called it a ‘vile bargain’.

quiz.q: What was the Prophet’s ﷺ reply on hearing his uncle’s anxiety?
o: I will pause the da‘wah for some days
I will carry on the da‘wah only in secret
If my uncle wishes I will leave Makkah
Even if they give the sun and moon I will not leave this path
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said, even if they bring the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left, he would not give up the da‘wah; either Allah will make it victorious, or he will perish in this path.

quiz.q: What did Abu Talib finally say on hearing the Prophet’s ﷺ reply?
o: Say what you wish, I will not hand you over to anyone
Wait some days, let me see the situation
Now see your own way yourself
Sit with Quraysh and come to a middle settlement
quiz.e: Seeing the Prophet’s ﷺ firmness and tears, Abu Talib’s doubt cleared; he said, ‘go, say what you wish, by Allah I will not hand you over to anyone’.

quiz.q: The reply ‘even if they give the sun and moon I will not leave’ is basically a proof of what?
o: Of the Prophet’s ﷺ extraordinary power and skill in speech and language
Of the firm support of his uncle Abu Talib
Of the sincerity of one who does not budge even for the world
Of the weak position inside the Quraysh leadership
quiz.e: However great the temptation, the one who moves not a hair’s breadth has no self-interest behind his claim; this steadfastness is itself a proof of truthfulness.

quiz.q: Why is Abu Talib’s request ‘enough, stop’ harder to handle than the enemy’s threat?
o: Abu Talib was far more powerful than Quraysh
Replying to the enemy’s threat was then completely forbidden
Because Abu Talib did not accept faith in the end
Saying ‘no’ is heavier under the soft pressure of a dear and affectionate person
quiz.e: An enemy’s scolding raises the stubbornness to resist; but turning away the pleading request of one who has shielded you all your life is much heavier.

quiz.q: Why did Abu Talib call the offer of ‘Umarah ibn al-Walid a ‘vile bargain’?
o: He would give his own son for rearing, his brother’s son for killing
‘Umarah ibn al-Walid was not at all good-looking and well built
Quraysh had also demanded a large sum of money in exchange
‘Umarah was in fact a close relative of his own
quiz.e: The proposal was that he would rear another’s son and hand over his own brother’s son, whom they would kill; such an unequal exchange was unimaginable to him.

quiz.q: When someone dear tells you in a soft voice to move away from the truth, what does the Prophet’s ﷺ reply teach?
o: To step back for the time being for some days
To always accept whatever dear ones say
To remain firm in truth even under the pressure of love
To fall completely silent to avoid argument
quiz.e: Even at the uncle’s pleading request the Prophet ﷺ said he would not leave the path even if given the sun and moon; the pressure of affection too cannot be a reason to leave the truth.

quiz.q: When obstacles come to someone’s good work, what lesson is there in Abu Talib’s last word?
o: To think many times before deciding to help anyone
To move quickly to a neutral position as soon as pressure comes
Once decided to stand by someone, not to waver under pressure
To stand by someone only if there is one’s own gain
quiz.e: Though falling into doubt, Abu Talib finally said, ‘I will not hand you over to anyone’; the real thing is to hold on to the pledge of support under pressure.

quiz.q: When pressure from family-society and truth come together, what is the priority?
o: Going wherever more people are going
Whatever increases honour in society
Choosing for the time being whatever is easiest
Not giving up truth even in exchange for a great worldly return
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ did not leave the path even in exchange for the sun and moon; worldly gain or the pressure of relatives cannot go above truth.

quiz.q: Why is the soft request of one’s dear ones harder to handle than an enemy’s threat?
o: Dear ones’ words have more argument
A scolding makes a person hard, weeping makes him soft
Dear ones’ words have to be heard more times
There is the chance of taking legal shelter against a scolding
quiz.e: Quraysh had understood that it could not be broken from outside; it had to be broken from within. So they went to Abu Talib.

quiz.q: In reply to the proposal ‘a year your gods, a year my Lord’, which surah was revealed?
o: Surah Bani Isra’il
Surah al-Kafirun
Surah al-Nasr
Surah al-Ma‘un
quiz.e: In reply to this proposal of worship by turns Surah al-Kafirun was revealed; ‘for you your religion and for me my religion’.

quiz.q: On hearing which verse did ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah suddenly put his hand on the Prophet’s ﷺ mouth and say ‘stop’?
o: A verse about the beginning of the creation of the heavens and earth
A verse of the stories of earlier prophets
A verse about the blessings of Paradise
A verse of the punishment of the thunderbolt of ‘Ad and Thamud
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ was reciting Surah Ha-Mim Sajdah; reaching the verse of warning of a punishment like the thunderbolt of ‘Ad and Thamud, ‘Utbah in fear asked him to stop.

quiz.q: What impossible demands did Quraysh put before the Prophet ﷺ?
o: To move mountains, make rivers flow and bring dead forefathers to life
To make a new idol and seat it inside the Ka‘bah
Only to leave Makkah
Only to carry on the da‘wah in secret
quiz.e: According to Surah Bani Isra’il 90–93 they demanded bringing out a spring, a garden of gold, moving mountains, bringing Qusayy ibn Kilab to life, sending down an angel and dropping a piece of the sky.

quiz.q: Among the four Quraysh leaders who came with the compromise proposal were
o: ‘Utbah, Shaybah, Abu Jahl and ‘Uqbah
al-Aswad, al-Walid, Umayyah and al-‘As ibn Wa’il
Abu Lahab, Mut‘im, al-Nadr and ‘Uqbah
Abu Sufyan, al-Harith, Shaybah and ‘Umarah ibn al-Walid
quiz.e: They said, in the whole affair you and we will become partners; both sides will get a share of the good.

quiz.q: The smallest proposal of Quraysh was
o: To give the da‘wah only secretly at night
To remove the poor Companions from the assembly
To touch their deities once
Only not to recite the Qur’an inside the Ka‘bah
quiz.e: He was not asked to give up prayer, Qur’an, or da‘wah; only to have one hand touch once. In exchange, all of Makkah.

quiz.q: By what address were the proposers of compromise called in Surah al-Zumar?
o: O ignorant ones
O transgressors
O possessors of blind hearts
O ascribers of falsehood
quiz.e: Verse 64 of Surah al-Zumar; the proposal had come from the most intelligent people of Makkah, yet Allah called them ignorant.

quiz.q: The two whom the Prophet ﷺ chose to give the adhan in Madinah were
o: Bilal and Abu Mahdhurah (RA)
Abu Bakr and Bilal (RA)
Zayd and Ibn Umm Maktum (RA)
Bilal and Ibn Umm Maktum (RA)
quiz.e: Hadith no. 617 of Sahih al-Bukhari; the one from whom a face was once turned away was the one seated in the duty of the adhan.

quiz.q: After whose words was the exception ‘those who are unable’ added to verse 95 of Surah al-Nisa’?
o: Ibn Umm Maktum (RA)
‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ud (RA)
Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)
Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA)
quiz.e: Hadith no. 4594 of Sahih al-Bukhari; he had said, O Messenger of Allah, I am blind. At once the exception was revealed.

quiz.q: What principle does the rejection of the proposal of ‘worship by turns’ with Surah al-Kafirun show?
o: In tawhid there is no bargaining or middle road
Temporary concessions can be made as needed
One should not speak to disbelievers at all
When such a proposal comes it is better to stay silent without replying
quiz.e: Agreeing to idol worship even for one year means giving up tawhid; in the question of creed there is no compromise, however short the time.

quiz.q: What is the significance of saying ‘I am only a human being, a messenger’ in reply to the miraculous demands?
o: The Prophet ﷺ was truly unable to fulfil these demands
The prophet’s job is not to create signs but to deliver the message
Showing signs was forbidden for him at that time
He was not willing to hear the demands
quiz.e: Sending down signs is Allah’s prerogative; the Messenger’s duty is to deliver the message. Showing miracles on request is not his job.

quiz.q: At the start of Surah ‘Abasa it is said ‘he frowned’, not ‘you frowned’; what is the significance?
o: The matter was really said about someone else
The correction came, yet the honour remained intact
The verse was revealed later
The matter was kept hidden in it
quiz.e: A few verses later the direct address returned; only the first statement was made from behind a veil.

quiz.q: What does verse 9 of Surah al-Qalam tell about the inner calculation of Quraysh?
o: They wanted him to stop the da‘wah completely
They wanted him to leave Makkah
They wanted him to be a little soft
They wanted him to ask forgiveness publicly
quiz.e: The statement of the verse, they want you to be a little soft, then they too will be soft. The rest would have happened by itself.

quiz.q: When a proposal of compromise comes, what will be the position of a Muslim in the matter of faith and creed?
o: To give some temporary concessions as the situation demands
Not to compromise in the question of core belief
To accept whatever the majority say
To avoid altogether the one who gives the proposal
quiz.e: Surah al-Kafirun shows there is no concession in tawhid even for a year; flexibility is allowed in conduct, not in creed.

quiz.q: If someone attaches a condition of showing a miraculous proof to the one giving the call to truth, what does this lesson teach?
o: If the condition is not fulfilled the da‘wah should be taken as void
When such a demand arises it is better to fall silent
Signs are in Allah’s hand; not by imposing conditions
It is the duty of the da‘i to fulfil and show every demand
quiz.e: Quraysh set conditions such as moving mountains and bringing the dead to life; the reply was, this is in Allah’s hand. Faith comes by considering the claimant’s proven honesty and reasoning, not by miracles on request.

quiz.q: ‘Religion is a private matter, keep it at home’ is really the new face of which old proposal?
o: Hand Muhammad over to us
The demand of moving the mountains
A year yours, a year mine
Do not go near the pilgrims
quiz.e: A proposal to split life into two; one part for Allah, another for someone else.

porbos.title: The Test of Three Questions • The Blueprint to Stop the Pilgrims • Final Word

blocks.1: Threats, temptation, compromise; nothing worked. Then Quraysh decided, let us take another path now. Let us put the man to a test. But how would they test! They themselves know nothing of prophethood. They have no scripture. No scholar. So they decided to go to those who have a heavenly Book.
blocks.2: Two Envoys on the Road to Yathrib
blocks.3: Two were chosen. al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt. Both clever men of Makkah; they knew how to put words in order. They set out toward Yathrib. The purpose, to meet the Jewish scholars there.
blocks.4: Arriving, they said, a man has stood up among us; he calls himself a prophet. You are People of the Book. You have a book, you have news of the earlier prophets. Teach us something by which the man can be tested.
blocks.6: The scholars conferred among themselves for a while. Then they said, ask three questions. One. Ask about those youths who were lost long ago; what is their story.
blocks.7: Two. Ask about the man who travelled from east to west; what is his news. Three. And ask, what is the Spirit (ruh). The three questions are like this. The first two are of history; events which no Arab knows, which are in no poem, in no tale. And the third is about a thing that is in every human being; yet no one knows its whereabouts. That is, the questions were chosen in such a way that there is no path to answer by using one’s wits.
blocks.8: Then the scholars gave the yardstick too. If he answers correctly, he is a prophet; follow him. And if he cannot, know that he is making things up.{{1}}
blocks.10: The two envoys returned to Makkah. They gave the news in the assembly of Quraysh. Then all together they went to the Prophet {{1}}. One by one they asked all three questions. The Prophet {{2}} said, I will answer tomorrow. The statement is natural. He knew revelation would come.
blocks.11: But one thing he did not say. In shaa Allah. The next morning came. Revelation did not come. The second day. The third day. A week passed. Fifteen days went by like this. Makkah began to laugh. They said, where is it, where is yesterday’s answer! And what passed over the Prophet {{1}} in these fifteen days, only he knows. He had said, I will answer tomorrow. And the heavens stayed silent.
blocks.12: Then the whole of Surah al-Kahf was revealed. The story of those youths in the cave came. The account of Dhu al-Qarnayn, who roamed east and west, came. And in the middle came a gentle correction
blocks.14: (O Prophet!) Never say about any matter, ‘I will do this tomorrow’. Except (say) ‘if Allah wills’. And when you forget, remember your Lord and say, I hope my Lord will guide me to something closer to right guidance than this.{{1}}
blocks.15: And the answer to the question of the Spirit came separately
blocks.17: (O Prophet!) They ask you about the Spirit. Say, the Spirit is a matter of my Lord’s command. The knowledge you have been given is only a little.{{1}}
blocks.19: Now place the three questions and three answers side by side. There were three questions. Three answers came too. But along with them came a fourth thing. A correction of his own by the one giving the answers.
blocks.20: If anyone were speaking on his own invention, would he stay silent for fifteen days! He would have fabricated an answer the very next morning. And would he announce his own mistake in his own mouth to everyone! In the very Book that he recites, his own correction is written. And he did not hide it; he recited it.
blocks.21: A liar does not leave behind a witness against himself.
blocks.23: The case of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith is different. He was one of the cleverest men of Quraysh. And he did a thing that no one else did. On trade business he had gone to al-Hirah; toward Iraq. Sitting there he had learned the old tales of Persia. The story of Rustam. The story of Isfandiyar. Tales of kings and emperors, of wars, heroism and love.
blocks.24: Then returning to Makkah he got to work. The Prophet {{1}} would sit in some gathering and recite the Qur’an. People listened quietly. After he got up and left, al-Nadr would go and sit at exactly that spot.
blocks.25: Then he would call people. He would say, come, sit. I will tell you a better tale than this. Better than Muhammad’s words. Do you catch the trick! He did not bring anything like the Qur’an in reply to the Qur’an. Nor did he refute anything with argument. He only sat beside it and set down an alternative. So that people would think, both are tales after all; one of Arabia, one of Persia.
blocks.26: And when his target was some particular person, the arrangement was even softer. If he sensed someone leaning toward Islam he would call him home. Feed him. Have songs sung to him. For this he had bought a singing slave-girl and kept her. Then he would say, look, this is better.{{1}}
blocks.27: And from this man’s very mouth came the statement that the Qur’an has preserved. He used to say, these are just the tales of the earlier peoples. That is, the same fable; old stories like Rustam and Isfandiyar. And he did not stop here. He said, if I wished I could say the like of it.
blocks.29: When Our verses are recited to them, they say, (well) we have heard! If we wished we could say the like of it. This (the Qur’an) is nothing but the fables of earlier people.{{1}}
blocks.31: He did not say, this is false. He said, if I wished I could do it too. But he did not wish. The man who went all the way to al-Hirah and learned tales did not once take up the pen to write one surah.
blocks.32: And what was the end of this man! At the field of Badr he was taken captive. And there his account was settled.{{1}}
blocks.33: Allah named this tactic in the Qur’an–
blocks.35: Among people there are some who, out of ignorance, buy such talk as would lead people astray from the path of Allah, make them heedless of Allah, and they ridicule the path of Allah. For them there is a punishment that will humiliate.{{1}}
blocks.37: The word is important here. He buys. That is, money is spent behind it. Keeping people distracted is an investment. Now to today. Today no one sits in the precinct of the Ka‘bah telling tales of Rustam. There is no need. The tale is now in the palm of our hand.
blocks.38: The sermon ended. People came out of the mosque. Stepping onto the road everyone took out a phone. Ten minutes later no one could say what the sermon was about. Al-Nadr no longer has to take the trouble of sitting. He now sits in the pocket.
blocks.39: And do you remember al-Nadr’s singing-girl! The arrangement to keep distracted the man who is leaning toward the truth. Today that too exists. A boy has repented. He is going to sleep at night with good intention. And just then, on the screen appears exactly the thing he was trying to give up. Not a coincidence. Someone has paid money and calculated what he will be shown. Al-Nadr bought a singer with money. Today people’s attention is bought with money.
blocks.40: So what is to be done! Against al-Nadr the Prophet {{1}} set up no counter-storytelling assembly. He did not stop reciting the Qur’an. He only carried on the work. And after a time people themselves decided which is a tale and which is life.
blocks.41: So take one task from today’s lesson. After the sermon or lesson ends, for at least ten minutes do not take out the phone. Let the word get the time to settle. Al-Nadr is waiting after all. Defeat him for at least ten minutes.
blocks.42: The three questions they themselves had selected and brought. The yardstick too was fixed by them. The answer came, and matched. Then they sat down to look for new questions. The matter is the same even today. Someone says, explain just this one thing; then I will accept.
blocks.43: When you explain, he raises the next. For the one who truly seeks, his questions stop one day. And for the one who does not want to accept, his questions never run out.
blocks.44: The Blueprint to Stop the Pilgrims
blocks.45: The Hajj season was drawing near again. From all Arabia people would come to Makkah. They would hear the Qur’an from the mouth of the Prophet {{1}}, then return to their own areas and spread the word. Quraysh could not let this happen.
blocks.46: They gathered at the house of al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Al-Walid said, come to one verdict. If each of you says a different thing, outsiders will understand that you are lying. They began weighing various labels. Shall we say poet? No, we know poetry; this is not poetry. Shall we say soothsayer? No, this is not the utterance of a soothsayer either. Shall we say mad? No, there is no sign of madness in it.
blocks.47: At last they settled on one statement. Al-Walid said, the closest is to say sorcerer. Because just as a sorcerer causes separation between father and son, between husband and wife, this one too is separating people from their father, brother and family.
blocks.48: The decision was, men would be posted on every road entering Makkah. The arriving pilgrims would be warned in advance; do not go near that man, he is a sorcerer.{{1}}
blocks.49: But the result was the opposite. Every pilgrim who was stopped on the road and warned, on entering Makkah he looked for that very man before anyone else. Returning, he told his tribe, there is a man in Makkah whom they forbade us to listen to.
blocks.50: In a single season the name of the Prophet {{1}} reached every tribe of Arabia. The publicity Quraysh wanted to stop spread by Quraysh’s own hands.
blocks.52: In today’s lesson we saw the da‘wah come from secret to open. That call from the hill of Safa; and the first blow came from the mouth of his own uncle Abu Lahab. The storm of mockery, slander and jeering; and in reply, the heavenly consolation. Delegation after delegation of Quraysh at Abu Talib’s; threats, temptation, a strange bargain. That declaration of not leaving the path even if given the sun and moon. Wealth, kingship, miraculous demands, worship by turns; and in reply Surah al-Kafirun. The test of three questions, and in reply the whole of Surah al-Kahf. And in trying to stop the pilgrims, instead spreading the name of the Prophet {{1}}.
blocks.53: One thing worth noting. The harshest blow of the open da‘wah came not from some stranger, but from an uncle. And the softest pressure came from another uncle; enough, now stop. Sometimes this soft request from one’s own is harder to handle than an enemy’s threat.
blocks.54: If truth had no price, people would not believe it. The price itself is the proof of truth’s sincerity. And in today’s lesson we saw one more thing. This struggle of fourteen hundred years ago has not ended. Only its face has changed.
blocks.55: That day the da‘wah began from one’s own house; and today our da‘wah does not even cross the door of the house. That day they said Mudhammam; today they say backdated. That day the pressure came through an uncle’s mouth; today it comes through the tears in a mother’s eyes. That day the proposal was a year yours, a year mine; today it has become the morning for Allah and the rest of the day for the account-book.
blocks.56: So let me end the lesson with a question. Quraysh did not ask the Prophet {{1}} to give up everything. They only wanted a little space. He did not give even that little. And we! Have we ever reckoned how much each one has taken from us!
blocks.57: When proposals and threats achieved nothing, Quraysh stooped to laying hands directly. In the next lesson we will see the torture and murder plots that came down upon the Prophet {{1}} himself.
blocks.59: Quraysh did not want everything. They wanted a little space. He did not give even that little. Today I will ask myself one question, who has taken how much space from my religion? Today I will take back one portion of that space, start with one deed, which from today I will not give up.

footnotes.0: Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham, 1/300–301; Tafsir al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir, introduction to Surah al-Kahf. On the sending of two envoys by Quraysh, the three questions of the Jewish scholars, and the background of the revelation of Surah al-Kahf. The event is narrated in the Seerah and tafsir books; there is discussion among the hadith scholars about its chain too. But the account of the People of the Cave and Dhu al-Qarnayn in Surah al-Kahf and the answer to the question of the Spirit in Surah Bani Isra’il are the Qur’an’s own statements.
footnotes.3: The three questions of Quraysh (the People of the Cave, Dhu al-Qarnayn and the Spirit), the verification on the advice of the Jewish scholars of Yathrib, and the incident of the revelation of Surah al-Kahf: Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham; Tafsir Ibn Kathir, introduction to Surah al-Kahf. There is variation in the narrations about how long revelation paused; in some places fifteen days, in others three or forty days are said. This account of the occasion of revelation is narrated in the Seerah and tafsir books, not in Sahih al-Bukhari or Muslim.
footnotes.4: On al-Nadr ibn al-Harith’s going to al-Hirah and learning Persian royal tales such as Rustam and Isfandiyar, sitting beside the gathering of the Prophet {{1}} and calling people over, and mocking the Qur’an as ‘tales of the earlier peoples’: Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham. Mention of this statement in the Qur’an: Surah al-An‘am 25; Surah al-Furqan 5; Surah al-Anfal 31. The chain of this narration of Ibn Ishaq is mursal. But the statement of calling the Qur’an ‘tales of the earlier peoples’ is in the Qur’an itself in several places; that much is definitive.
footnotes.6: The exegetes have mentioned that verse 31 of Surah al-Anfal was revealed concerning the statement of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith; see Ibn Ishaq; Tafsir al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir. The phrase ‘asatir al-awwalin’, or tales of the earlier peoples, has come in several places in the Qur’an; such as Surah al-An‘am 25, Surah al-Furqan 5, Surah al-Qalam 15. This account of the occasion of revelation is mursal through Ibn Ishaq and tafsir-based; the statement of the verse, however, is definitive.
footnotes.7: On the arrest of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith at Badr and his end see Sirat Ibn Hisham; Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah. The account of al-Nadr being taken captive at Badr and killed at a place called al-Safra is narrated in Ibn Ishaq and the Maghazi books; the chain is mursal. The general matter of the captives of Badr, however, has come in sahih hadith too.
footnotes.9: On the occasion of revelation of verse 6 of Surah Luqman, Ibn ‘Abbas, Ibn Mas‘ud and Jabir (RA) have mentioned al-Nadr ibn al-Harith; see the tafsir of Imam al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir; Sirat Ibn Hisham, 1/300–301. The statement of Ibn Mas‘ud (RA) in explanation of ‘lahw al-hadith’ is narrated through a sahih chain as mawquf. But the account that the verse was revealed specifically concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith is mentioned in tafsir; the chain is mursal or weak.
footnotes.10: Ibn Ishaq; Sirat Ibn Hisham 1/270–271. On the meeting of Quraysh at the house of al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah before the Hajj season, the discussion of what label to give the Prophet {{1}}, the final settlement on ‘sorcerer, who causes separation between father and son’, and the posting of men on the roads to warn the arriving pilgrims. Ibn Ishaq’s narration is mursal. But the part about al-Walid’s acknowledgement of the Qur’an and the revelation of Surah al-Muddaththir concerning it is narrated also in al-Hakim’s al-Mustadrak and al-Bayhaqi’s Dala’il al-Nubuwwah via Ibn ‘Abbas (RA).

quiz.q: Whom did Quraysh send to Yathrib to collect questions to test the Prophet ﷺ?
o: Abu Jahl and Umayyah
‘Utbah and Shaybah
al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and ‘Uqbah
al-Walid and al-‘As ibn Wa’il
quiz.e: al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt were sent to the Jewish scholars of Yathrib, to bring questions fit to test the Prophet ﷺ.

quiz.q: What was the subject of the three questions given by the Jewish scholars?
o: What are the rulings of prayer, fasting and zakat
What are the Hour, Paradise and Hell like
The lineage of Arabia, tribal chiefs and the system of rule
The youths of the cave, the traveller east and west, and the Spirit
quiz.e: The youths of the cave (the People of the Cave), Dhu al-Qarnayn who roamed east and west, and what the Spirit is; if he could answer these three questions he is a prophet, if he could not, he is making it up.

quiz.q: In answer to the three questions of Quraysh, which surah was mainly revealed?
o: Surah al-Kahf
Surah al-Rum
Surah Yusuf
Surah al-Naml
quiz.e: The accounts of the People of the Cave and Dhu al-Qarnayn come in Surah al-Kahf; the answer to the question of the Spirit comes in verse 85 of Surah Bani Isra’il.

quiz.q: In verse 31 of Surah al-Anfal, the claim they made on hearing the Qur’an was
o: This cannot be the word of any human
We do not understand even a letter of it
If we wished we could say the like of it
This was taken from our poets
quiz.e: The statement is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith’s; he did not say it is false, he said if I wished I could too. But he never wrote anything.

quiz.q: What does the pause of revelation for not saying ‘in shaa Allah’ and the correction coming in al-Kahf teach?
o: An answer to a question cannot be kept for the next day
Statements about future work should be tied to Allah’s will
It was not right to answer the questions asked by the Jewish scholars
Whether revelation comes or not depends on the kind of question
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said ‘I will tell tomorrow’ without adding ‘in shaa Allah’; the pause of revelation and the revelation of al-Kahf 23–24 teach that one must speak of tomorrow on condition of Allah’s will.

quiz.q: What was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith’s trick of narrating ‘royal tales of Persia’ really?
o: Making Quraysh aware by teaching old history
Showing off his own scholarship and knowledge in the assembly
Moving people away from the Qur’an with flashy tales
Running publicity and promotion for trade routes with Persia
quiz.e: As soon as the Prophet ﷺ finished reciting the Qur’an he would sit beside and call people and tell tales; the aim was to lighten the Qur’an’s effect. The Qur’an called their very statement ‘tales of the earlier peoples’.

quiz.q: The fifteen days’ silence in reply to the three questions is called in the lesson a proof of what?
o: That the questions of Quraysh were difficult
That the Jewish scholars chose the right questions
That communication in Makkah was difficult then
That the words were not of his own making
quiz.e: If speaking on his own invention, an answer could have been put up the next morning; and no one publishes his own correction.

quiz.q: What was the nature of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith’s tactic?
o: Proving truth false with argument
Making truth seem unnecessary
Frightening the followers of truth
Forcing truth to be kept hidden
quiz.e: He did not say the Qur’an is wrong; he sat beside it and set down an alternative, so that people would think both are tales.

quiz.q: When promising to do some work in the future, what should be said according to this lesson?
o: Saying it by adding ‘if Allah wills I will do it’
Evading the answer and turning the talk
Giving a fully certain promise
Not fixing the time of when the work will be
quiz.e: Because ‘I will tell tomorrow’ was said without ‘in shaa Allah’, revelation paused and Surah al-Kahf 23–24 was revealed; one must learn to speak of tomorrow on condition of Allah’s will.

quiz.q: When people are drawn with a flashy alternative beside good speech, what caution comes from al-Nadr’s tactic?
o: To recognise attempts to divert the heart under cover of entertainment
Entertainment means harm, taking this for granted is safe
All kinds of stories and tales should be avoided
Only the words of a known speaker are safe to hear
quiz.e: Al-Nadr sat beside the Qur’an gathering telling flashy tales so that people would turn away from the Qur’an; an attractive alternative is not always harmless.

quiz.q: Before the Hajj season, what label did Quraysh decide to give the Prophet ﷺ?
o: Poet
Sorcerer
Soothsayer
Majnun or mad
quiz.e: In al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah’s meeting, all labels, poet, soothsayer, madman, were dropped and finally ‘sorcerer, who causes separation in the family’ was settled.

quiz.q: Why did Quraysh’s tactic of warning the pilgrims give the opposite result?
o: The men Quraysh posted could not block the pilgrims’ way properly
Hearing the prohibition, people became curious and rather looked for him
The arriving pilgrims did not believe Quraysh at all
That season there was a much smaller gathering of people in Makkah
quiz.e: Hearing ‘do not go near that man’, the arriving people first went and looked for him, then returning to their own tribes spoke of him; so in a single season his name spread over all Arabia.

quiz.q: Why did Quraysh finally drop ‘poet/soothsayer/madman’ and choose ‘sorcerer’?
o: The word ‘sorcerer’ sounded more terrible than the other three
al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah himself knew sorcery
The Arabs of that time believed in sorcery the most
Like a sorcerer, the da‘wah too was separating people from the family
quiz.e: The Qur’an matched neither poetry nor the utterance of soothsayers; finally they chose a slander that fits the practical result; hearing the Qur’an many were leaving family and coming to Islam.

quiz.q: When opponents try to stop the spread of truth with false labels, what hope does this lesson give?
o: The spread of truth stops completely thereby
People then no longer want to verify anything
Once a false label sticks it lasts forever
Prohibition often increases curiosity and spreads the message
quiz.e: The propaganda ‘sorcerer, do not go near him’ gave the opposite result; arriving people first looked for him, and his name spread over all Arabia.

quiz.q: When false slander is spread, what hope does this lesson give about the spread of truth?
o: Slander covers truth forever
If Allah wills, truth spreads by the very hand of slander
To avoid slander, staying completely silent is better
If no reply is given, truth is eventually lost
quiz.e: The propaganda of warning the pilgrims instead carried the Prophet’s ﷺ name to all Arabia; if Allah wills, even the opponent’s tactic becomes a vehicle of the da‘wah.

quiz.q: In what pattern did Quraysh’s tactics change in the face of the open da‘wah?
o: From start to finish there were only weapons and threats of war
First temptation, then complete silence
First pressure, then temptation, then compromise and testing
Only repeated complaints to Abu Talib
quiz.e: When threats at Abu Talib’s did not work, they offered the temptation of wealth and leadership, then asked for the compromise of worship by turns, and finally went to test him with three questions.

quiz.q: When opposition becomes intense, what is the believer to do, according to this lesson?
o: Carry on the da‘wah with patience, the result is in Allah’s hand
Sit with the opponents and compromise
Quietly fold up all the preaching
Go on the counter-attack and answer in harsh words
quiz.e: Despite threats, temptation and slander the Prophet ﷺ carried on the da‘wah; ‘either Allah will make it victorious, or I will perish in this path’; the result is Allah’s.
